The strongest likely cause is render pressure, not score validation: BlindEvaluationPanel renders up to 32 responses and 4 MiB of text without a height/overflow bound in App.tsx:3761-3771 and styles.css:1164-1215. Every score change updates state and rerenders the entire response tree. The separate ArenaResultsSurface score path at App.tsx:2795 and 2873 is local-only and similarly rerenders response cards, but its text is bounded. The score handler at App.tsx:3678-3685 uses fixed 1–5 options, token-keyed state, and no Tauri invoke, so no invalid index, null current item, or direct invoke exception was found. State transitions are loading -> idle/locked/error; idle -> preparing -> empty/prepared/locked/error; prepared score edits remain prepared; lock -> locked/error. RunsView hides attempt evidence while prepared and reveals it after lock at App.tsx:3125-3298. Backend preparation/locking is validated and immutable: evaluation.rs:56-265 and 275-390; storage.rs:1878-1910; migration 0004 only stores immutable JSON. No duplicate mutation, unstable score key, stale route key, malformed score shape, or blind-token corruption was evidenced. Lock invokes synchronous Rust storage through bridge.ts:875-900 and commands.rs:930-950, so lock-time blocking is a secondary risk, not the score-change trigger. No React error boundary or global renderer error hook exists; an actual render exception would have no in-app recovery. The safe fix boundary is to bound or virtualize response presentation while retaining full verified artifacts, then add explicit renderer recovery only if a captured exception proves necessary; preserve token validation, size limits, plain-text rendering, immutable storage, and blind identity controls. Runtime/browser reproduction was not possible here: ollama process was running, but ollama command and port 11434 listener were absent; no browser/component harness or native TUI was used.
